claim: Across fork-based software families in Android, .NET and JavaScript there is little code integration between mainline and variant forks in either direction.
Only about 11% of mainline-variant fork pairs ever exchange code, and mainline-to-variant flow exceeds variant-to-mainline.
Across 18 years of BSD history the mean lag to port a peer project's patch was roughly 725 to 944 days and did not decline over time.
git cherry-pick failed on 64.4% of bug-fix pull requests across divergent variant fork pairs due to structural drift and refactoring.

No downstream patching strategy wins on all axes: rebasing distributions get zero porting delay but inherit essentially all mainline bugs, while conservative cherry-pickers inherit far fewer bugs but port slowest.
Among several hundred significant open-source forks, very few ever merge back with the original project.
The LibreOffice fork showed no stagnation after the fork because it captured the most active long-term committers from OpenOffice.org.
Better modularity and more centralized management predict more contributions and higher pull-request acceptance in open-source projects.
Most hard forks evolved accidentally out of social forks rather than being deliberately planned.
Dormant npm packages accumulate outdated dependencies and unpatched vulnerabilities.
An analysis of 174 real malicious packages across npm, PyPI and RubyGems found typosquatting and maintainer account compromise as dominant infection vectors.

authors: Huang, Xia, Chen, Zhou, Guo, Peng
claim: About half of license-declaring forks violated license modification terms and the overwhelming majority of obligating commits lacked required modification notices.
FID carries a sample-size-dependent bias whose magnitude differs per model, so model rankings can invert on bias alone.

FID has poor sample complexity and gives inconsistent results as sample size varies, and its normality assumption on Inception embeddings is unjustified; CMMD is proposed as an unbiased distribution-free alternative.
KID is an unbiased MMD-based generative metric that makes no Gaussian assumption about the feature distribution.
Merely aligning the ImageNet class histogram of generated images substantially improves FID without improving perceived image quality.
Aliased image resizing and JPEG compression shift FID enough to change model rankings.
Deep network features (LPIPS) outperform classical metrics at matching human perceptual similarity judgments.
DISTS separates texture similarity from structure similarity using spatial averages of VGG feature maps and is deliberately tolerant to texture resampling.
Correlations between convolutional feature maps (Gram matrices) form an effective texture representation.
CLIP embeddings prioritize content over style, and a style-specific descriptor outperforms CLIP on style retrieval benchmarks.
DreamSim is designed to capture mid-level semantic and layout similarity and to look past low-level colour and texture differences.
DINO self-supervised embeddings preserve instance-specific subject detail better than CLIP image embeddings for subject-fidelity evaluation.
ImageNet-trained convolutional networks are biased toward texture rather than shape.
